readOnlyDefinition: readOnly = no persistent-state write AND no network AND no LLM billing AND no CLI->external process spawn (output constancy over time is deliberately NOT part of it)
note: Hand-authored SOURCE OF TRUTH for the read-only argv surface. It is the input to
`scripts/generate-readonly-whitelist.ts`, which verifies every entry against the live
Commander registry and emits `contracts/readonly-argv-whitelist.json`. Nothing imports
the generated file: it is data, read through the filesystem by the whitelist loader.
A token wrapped in angle brackets (<name>) is a placeholder; `params` carries its
constraint. Required-ness is NOT declared here - it is introspected from the registry
(a mandatory option, or a required positional), so it cannot drift.
MEASURED DEVIATIONS from the rid-035 PRD table (each reproduced against the real CLI,
never inferred): `peaks project dashboard --json` and `peaks request show <rid> --role
<role> --json` both exit 1 with MISSING_REQUIRED_OPTION, because `--project` is a
MANDATORY option on those two commands. The PRD listing omitted it. Those two entries
therefore carry `--project <project>`. That is exactly the evidence for the rule this
surface exists to encode: the whitelist key must be the FULL argv, flags included.
`peaks session list --json` is the mirror case - it accepts only `--json`.
EXCLUDED AFTER MEASUREMENT: `peaks project dashboard --json --project <project>`.
The PRD lists it as the third curated argv. The three-layer proof says it is NOT
read-only: run with the layer-B preload inside a real CLI process, it makes exactly
one `node:child_process.execFileSync` call (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, reached
through `findProjectRoot`), reproducibly, in this repository as well as in a fixture.
That violates the fourth clause of this file's `readOnlyDefinition`, and §11 of the
design says every argv in the surface must pass all three layers - so it is out of the
whitelist rather than special-cased inside it. `readonly-proof.test.ts` keeps the
measurement as a live arm, so the exclusion is reproduced on every run instead of
being asserted here. Lifting the spawn (or amending the definition to admit read-only
git queries) is a separate, user-confirmed change.
